title: Rupee stress episodes, scored by pressure markers

rows.label: 1991 BoP crisis
rows.mainStress: Reserve exhaustion, gold pledge, two-step devaluation
rows.rupeeMove: roughly 18-19% devaluation in July 1991, then market unification near Rs 31-32/$ by 1993
rows.externalGap: BoP financing crisis, import compression, very low usable reserves
rows.reserves: only a few weeks of imports before the rescue package
rows.flowsDollarOil: external borrowing dried up; Gulf war oil shock added pressure
rows.policyResponse: gold pledge, IMF support, LERMS, then 1993 market-linked rate
rows.dataCoverage: historical event data plus RBI reserve/BOP history

rows.label: 2013 taper tantrum
rows.mainStress: Record current-account deficit plus global dollar/rate shock
rows.reserves: reserve drawdown and emergency dollar funding measures
rows.flowsDollarOil: foreign money left EMs after the Fed taper signal
rows.policyResponse: rate/liquidity tightening, import curbs and FCNR(B) deposit window
rows.dataCoverage: RBI BOP/intervention/FPI plus FRED/BIS market series

rows.label: 2008 global crisis
rows.mainStress: Global funding shock and portfolio outflows
rows.rupeeMove: sharp depreciation as global risk appetite collapsed
rows.externalGap: external financing pressure, not a 1991-style current-account collapse
rows.reserves: large reserve drawdown from the pre-crisis peak
rows.flowsDollarOil: risk-off dollar demand and FII outflows
rows.policyResponse: RBI sold dollars, eased liquidity and cut rates as growth slowed

rows.label: 1966 devaluation
rows.mainStress: Peg became hard to defend after war, drought and aid stress
rows.rupeeMove: official rate moved from 4.76 to 7.50 per dollar
rows.externalGap: aid suspension, food imports and foreign-exchange shortage
rows.reserves: pre-modern reserve data are patchier than post-1990 series
rows.flowsDollarOil: not a portfolio-flow crisis; this was a pegged-rate and financing crisis
rows.policyResponse: one-time official devaluation under Bretton Woods
rows.dataCoverage: historical event sources; not comparable monthly market data

rows.label: 2022 Fed-oil-dollar shock
rows.mainStress: Fed hikes, strong dollar, expensive oil and RBI defence
rows.rupeeMove: rupee weakened through the year while the dollar surged globally
rows.externalGap: oil import bill and wider goods deficit raised dollar demand
rows.reserves: reserves fell as the RBI sold dollars and valuation effects hit
rows.flowsDollarOil: global dollar strength plus high crude after Russia's invasion of Ukraine
rows.policyResponse: spot intervention, rate hikes and liquidity management

rows.label: 2025-26 forward defence
rows.mainStress: FPI outflows and heavy forward-market defence despite large reserves
rows.rupeeMove: rupee moved near Rs 95/$ by June 2026
rows.externalGap: current-account deficit modest versus past crisis years
rows.reserves: monthly reserves near $686bn in May 2026, weekly total near $667bn by 26 Jun
rows.flowsDollarOil: FPI outflows of about $13.3bn in Mar 2026 and $7.3bn in Apr
rows.policyResponse: spot dollar sales and a net forward book near -$100bn
rows.dataCoverage: latest RBI DBIE workbooks through Apr-Jun 2026 depending on series

rows.label: 1997-98 Asia/sanctions
rows.rupeeMove: rupee weakened, but avoided an East-Asia-style collapse
rows.externalGap: current-account pressure was present but not the main rupture
rows.reserves: reserves provided more room than in 1991
rows.flowsDollarOil: regional contagion and risk aversion mattered more than oil
rows.policyResponse: managed depreciation, intervention and tighter liquidity
rows.dataCoverage: post-1993 market data available, but early FPI detail is thinner

rows.label: 2018 oil-EM selloff
rows.mainStress: Oil price rise, Fed tightening and emerging-market selloff
rows.rupeeMove: rupee weakened, but without a 1991 or 2013 funding break
rows.externalGap: oil and imports widened external pressure
rows.reserves: RBI used reserves to smooth the move
rows.flowsDollarOil: higher crude and stronger dollar drove the stress

metadata.method: Curated crisis scorecard. Score is an editorial severity marker, not a statistical model: higher values indicate more simultaneous stress across rupee fall/devaluation, external deficit, reserve pressure, hot-money or dollar shock, oil shock and policy/intervention stress.
metadata.caveat: Early episodes are historical event rows with patchier monthly data. Post-1993 episodes are more directly comparable because market INR/USD, reserves, FPI and intervention data are available.
